description:
Estudiantes de Biotecnología en el reto "Earth System Trend Detective". Usamos datos de la NASA para detectar eutrofización en aguas locales. ¡Buscamos diseñadores UI/UX, analistas de datos o creadores de contenido!

Biotech students monitoring local water eutrophication.
summary:
EcoStream Sgo is a water surveillance and terrestrial-satellite cross-validation platform designed to detect and mitigate floods, eutrophication, and harmful cyanobacterial blooms in the Dulce River (Santiago del Estero Capital, Argentina; -27.7850, -64.2450). Addressing the Earth System Trend Detective challenge, our tool evaluates 20 years (2006–2026) of NASA satellite observations alongside simulated in-situ IoT biosensor telemetry and geotagged citizen photography. 
By isolating river water with optical masks and applying a 95% confidence statistical filter (p < 0.05), EcoStream identifies what variables are changing, where they occur, by how much, and whether trends are statistically significant. Aligning climatic triggers, satellite heatmaps, and real-time water chemistry metrics (pH, turbidity, temperature, BOD, COD, phenols) into a four-level Cyanobacteria Traffic Light Scale, EcoStream prevents ecological collapse and triggers circular mitigation using floating Biochar barriers made from local agricultural waste
details:
What does it do and how does it work?
EcoStream Sgo is an early-warning environmental surveillance and terrestrial-satellite cross-validation (Ground-Truthing) platform built for the Dulce River Capital (-27.7850, -64.2450). It monitors and mitigates two interconnected threats: intense rain-driven river flooding and toxic cyanobacterial eutrophication. By aligning satellite observations with local water measurements by date and exact geographic coordinates, it translates complex 20-year environmental trends into an actionable four-level Hydro-Cyano Traffic Light Scale (Hidrocianosemáforo) and flood alert system for citizens and local authorities.

Our platform cross-validates complementary variables across three levels:

  1. Macro Layer (NASA Satellites — Climatic Triggers & Optical Effects): Using optical water/vegetation masking (NDWI/NDVI) to isolate the river channel and discard land false positives, our system evaluates 20 years (2006–2026) of daily data. It tracks climatic triggers—air temperature (T2M >35°C), relative humidity (RH2M <35%), solar irradiance (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN >6.5–7.5 kWh/m²/day), and heavy rainfall (PRECTOTCORR 30–50 mm/24h)—alongside algal biomass indicators (Chlorophyll-a 10–15 mg/m³ and modern NASA PACE hyperspectral data). A 95% confidence statistical filter (p < 0.05) isolates sustained long-term trends from normal weather fluctuations.
  2. Meso Layer (In-Situ IoT Biosensor — Physical & Chemical Effects): Using simulated telemetry in our current digital prototype (Phase 1), local stations track rising water levels (flood early warning) and real-time water chemistry: alkalinity (pH >8.5 driven by massive cyanobacterial CO₂ consumption via the Calvin cycle), turbidity (>20–30 NTU), water temperature (24–26°C), BOD (>5–10 mg/L), COD (>20–40 mg/L), and phenols (>0.001–0.002 mg/L).
  3. Micro Layer (Citizen Science): Geotagged shoreline photos provide direct surface confirmation and exact coordinates.

What benefits and intended impact does it have?
EcoStream protects public health, prevents aquatic oxygen depletion (anoxia), and mitigates flood and agricultural runoff damage in Santiago del Estero. Our 4-stage roadmap scales from the current Hackathon digital prototype (Stage 1) to 5 solar monitoring stations and 100 kg of lab-tested biochar (Stage 2), pilot river deployment in Santiago del Estero (Stage 3), and provincial institutional integration (Stage 4). By leveraging free NASA open data, open-source software, and unexploited local agricultural waste, a complete field pilot requires an estimated investment of only $1,250 USD (covering web/cloud hosting $50, 5 river sensor stations $450, double-drum biochar production and floating barriers $300, laboratory water-quality validation $250, and community workshops $200).

How is your project creative?
Instead of stopping at passive satellite monitoring, EcoStream closes the environmental loop through circular biotechnology and community design. We created the Hydro-Cyano Traffic Light Scale (Hidrocianosemáforo)—an intuitive four-level visual alert system combining flood risk and cyanobacterial toxicity—and paired it with floating HDPE geotextile barriers filled with Biochar produced locally via pyrolysis (450°C) of Santiago del Estero agricultural waste. These modular barriers rise and fall with river flood levels to adsorb nitrates, phosphates, phenols, and cyanotoxins without harmful chemical algicides, later turning into nutrient-rich compost for regional reforestation.

What factors did our team consider?
Our team specifically considered:

  1. Elimination of Satellite False Positives: Using optical water/vegetation masking (NDWI/NDVI) and three-layer ground-truthing (p < 0.05) so riverbanks and normal seasonal changes are never mistaken for blooms or floods.
  2. Extreme Climate & Hydrological Interactions: Linking heatwaves (>35°C), low humidity (<35%), and heavy storms (30–50 mm/24h) that wash agricultural nutrients into the Dulce River.
  3. Economic Viability & Sustainability: Designing a low-cost ($1,250 USD) pilot powered by free NASA open data and local crop residues so it is financially realistic for regional deployment.
  4. Public Accessibility: Translating complex NetCDF4 and CSV datasets into simple, actionable safety precautions for local residents, fishermen, and authorities.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software used:

  • NASA Data APIs & Formats: NASA POWER REST API (daily CSV time series), NASA Earthdata / Giovanni, NASA AppEEARS, and NetCDF4 (.nc) satellite data processing.
  • Software, App Design & Analytics: Interactive web/mobile application UI prototypes designed in Canva for Hydro-Cyano Traffic Light alerts and flood/bloom heatmaps, combined with statistical trend validation (p < 0.05).
  •  Visual Studio Code, Python, HTML, render, github

NASA AppEEARS / Terra MODIS (MOD13Q1 NDVI & NDWI)
